record.paper_title: Results and open problems in matchings in regular graphs
record.original_question: Let G(2n,r) be the class of simple r-regular graphs on 2n vertices, let phi(k,G) be the number of k-matchings in G, let K_{r,r} be the complete bipartite r-regular graph on 2r vertices, and let qK_{r,r} be the disjoint union of q copies of K_{r,r}. Is it true, for every r, q, and k = 1,...,qr, that qK_{r,r} maximizes the number of k-matchings among all simple r-regular graphs on 2qr vertices, equivalently Theta(k,qr,r) = phi(k,qK_{r,r})?

evidence.quote: The upper matching conjecture, abbreviated as UMC, states [23] Θ(k, qr, r) = φ(k, qKr,r) for k = 1, . . . , qr.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{G}(2n,r)$ denote the class of simple $r$-regular graphs on $2n$ vertices. For a graph $G$ and a non-negative integer $k$, let $\varphi(k,G)$ denote the number of $k$-matchings in $G$ (i.e., sets of $k$ pairwise vertex-disjoint edges), and define
$$\Theta(k,n,r) = \max_{G \in \mathcal{G}(2n,r)} \varphi(k,G).$$
Let $K_{r,r}$ denote the complete bipartite $r$-regular graph on $2r$ vertices, and for a positive integer $q$, let $qK_{r,r}$ denote the disjoint union of $q$ copies of $K_{r,r}$, which is an $r$-regular simple graph on $2qr$ vertices.

Prove or disprove: for every positive integers $r$ and $q$ and every $k \in \{1,2,\ldots,qr\}$,
$$\Theta(k,qr,r) = \varphi(k, qK_{r,r}).$$
Equivalently, $qK_{r,r}$ maximizes the number of $k$-matchings among all simple $r$-regular graphs on $2qr$ vertices.
artifact.status_search_result: Davies, Jenssen, and Perkins (J. Combin. Theory Ser. B, 2021; arXiv:2004.06695) proved the Upper Matching Conjecture for all sufficiently large $n$ as a function of the degree $r$: for each fixed $r$ there exists $n_0(r)$ such that the conjecture holds for $n \geq n_0(r)$. The conjecture in full generality (all $q$, $r$, $k$) does not appear to be fully settled.

status_evidence.title: A proof of the Upper Matching Conjecture for large graphs
status_evidence.snippet: For every d and large enough n divisible by 2d, a union of n/(2d) copies of K_{d,d} maximizes the number of matchings of size k for each k over all d-regular graphs on n vertices.
status_evidence.claim: The Upper Matching Conjecture has been proved for sufficiently large graphs as a function of the degree.

status_evidence.title: The Upper Matching Conjecture (2008) — D. West
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture page describing the original UMC of Friedland, Krop, and Markström.
status_evidence.claim: The UMC was posed as an open problem by Friedland, Krop, and Markström.
